title: Northern man shot twice, autopsy shows
article: A father and grandfather at Gods Lake Narrows - armed with a weapon - was shot twice by an RCMP officer early Tuesday in front of the site of a tragic fire that broke out just hours before.

And for the first time, the province's top RCMP officer called in an outside police force to investigate a police-involved shooting. As well, a respected elder at the northern community has now been named as an official observer during the investigation into the shooting.
An autopsy at the St. Boniface General Hospital performed on Wednesday confirmed that Paul Leonard Duck, 52, was struck twice by bullets and died as a result.

The Saskatoon Police Service, which was asked by assistant RCMP commissioner Bill Robinson to head the investigation into the RCMP shooting at this northern community, said in a statement that Duck was rushed to the local nursing station where he was pronounced dead.

Saskatoon police say two Gods Lake Narrows RCMP officers were guarding the site of a house fire - which claimed the lives of Demus James and his two young great-grandchildren, Kaylene Okemow, 3, and Tron Kirkness, 1, on Monday at about 11 a.m. - when "the members were confronted by an armed male subject.
"One of the RCMP members discharged his firearm."
Saskatoon police said no other details will be released until the investigation progresses.
Community members and Chief Peter Watt said two groups of youth were fighting when Duck became involved.
The community members said Duck fired his shotgun into the air to break up the fight and began following the youth just before he was shot.
Duck was married for 23 years and had four children, one of whom was adopted, and five grandchildren.
Henry Nazzie, a band councillor at the reserve, said he has been told that people who were near the shooting heard police telling Duck to drop his weapon before the shooting.
Nazzie said Duck's body is expected to be flown back to the community on Friday with a funeral planned for Monday.
Robinson said he can't comment on the shooting because another police force is leading the investigation. But Robinson said that doesn't stop him from calling it "a tragedy.
"This isn't just a tragedy for the family (of the shooting victim), but also a terrible tragedy for our members," he said.
"They'll have to live with having taken someone's life for the rest of their lives."
RCMP spokeswoman Sgt. Line Karpish said the force's employee assistance program has already begun working with the officer. Karpish said the officer has been removed from the community.
